I even said before that in the soccer field I saw people being treated and attended by -- doing the triage and by their own relatives in the open at the soccer field. I wouldn't call that a war hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Sir, I'm using a terminology that's not my own but from an author, but let's say medical clinic or let's say medical facility.

utterances.speaker: DIEGO ENRIQUE ARRIA
utterances.text: It reminds me of President Izetbegovic gave us a luncheon in Sarajevo and the menu said war soup, and it was almost like hot water. Probably is the closest thing to a hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: My question is: In the mandate of your mission, you did not go to the war hospital or the entity referred to as the war hospital and that didn't evolve into your mandate. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DIEGO ENRIQUE ARRIA
utterances.text: Everything was in our mandate. Unfortunately, I have failed to express forcefully what I meant. Our mandate encompassed anything and everything. I mean, at the same time there -- as I told you, there was no hospital, like there were no schools, there was no police, there was no army. There were just people suffering.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay. Can I ask directly: You didn't go to this war hospital during the time period you were in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DIEGO ENRIQUE ARRIA
utterances.text: We never saw anyone. There was no war hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Sir, then might I also ask you: Did you receive military briefings about the Bosnian -- from Bosnia-Herzegovina, their army, or the presence of their army whatsoever in Srebrenica municipality or city prior to your mission?

utterances.speaker: DIEGO ENRIQUE ARRIA
utterances.text: Never. I mean, we were so objective, Ms. Sellers, Your Honours, that the Bosnian ambassador to the United Nations, Sacirbey, presented himself to Zagreb, and I refused to let him in our helicopter to fly to Sarajevo. Because I said we are a United Nations mission, Security Council mission, and if you come in it would give the wrong impression what we are trying to do. Actually, it wasn't a very pleasant experience, but I as the head of the mission told him under no circumstances can you come in. And again, when we were in Zagreb he tried to enter a meeting where we were discussing with Morillon and Wahlgren, and I stood up and asked Ambassador Sacirbey to please leave the room. Along with my colleague, and he was representing that the country was suffering. But we were very sensitive to the issue that we should be very even-handed and objective. I want you to know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you for that information.

utterances.speaker: DIEGO ENRIQUE ARRIA
utterances.text: I never got any meetings -- to begin with, Ms. Sellers, there was no army. There was no army. The only general I heard his name was Halilovic. The rest, like I said to you before, looked to me and to the mission, like the Maquis during World War II, or the resistance in other parts of the world. But an army as such with ranks and so forth, never during my life. Not during our stay there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. How much more, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a couple of videos that I would like to show. And I don't want to ask the Ambassador -- we have to keep some questions a bit briefer, but there are some questions that I do need to move through. And I still would like to finish by today. I have already eliminated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. But we have a plenary at 4.00 and as chairman of the Rules Committee I have still got to do a lot of work, and we have been sitting for -- Ambassador, I've done my best to try and accommodate you. Would it be --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For you to decide, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I know that, but that's not in our style to disappoint anyone. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I just say, in the spirit of being helpful, in the moment I have no re-examination. And I would ask Ms. Sellers to consider really whether these videos are really going to be something which this witness can help with and if it's really worth bringing him back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We'll see that in due course, Your Honour, whether it's really worth it if this ambassador has to stay until tomorrow to see a video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What time are you flying, in the morning or in the afternoon, if I may ask?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was flying in the morning, Your Honour, but I believe this is such an important thing that I will be willing to stay as long as you wish me to stay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because at this stage, I mean, it would be very un-Orthodox on our part to stop you and say no or to pre-empt the issue that Mr. Jones has just raised. But we have been sitting for almost two hours now, one hour, 45 minutes, and I wouldn't like to put undue pressure on anyone. Ambassador, do you mind coming back again? Tomorrow we are sitting in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the morning, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, in the afternoon we are sitting tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have been trying in the meantime to see if we could shift the sitting to the morning, but I'm told it's not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I say, Your Honour, I skipped at least half a dozen exhibits and I tried to go quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know. Mr. Jones, if you want to visit those on cross -- on re-examination, we'll give you all the opportunity. Yes, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But -- all right. We'll have to stop here, also to give everyone a rest, a well-deserved rest. And we'll continue tomorrow, Ambassador. I'm sure that you will be taken care of, and I thank you so much for understanding. Tomorrow we are sitting in the afternoon. Is that correct? We are still sitting -- we haven't managed to -- all right. And we'll continue from there. Thank you so much. Bye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 6th day of December, 2005, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.21 p.m.,
